title: Water-Based Primer Scheme for Lower Shell Repair Areas
abstract: A proposal to qualify a water-borne primer for lower shell repair work, driven by solvent emission limits at repair stations rather than by the chromate restriction that shaped the current scheme.

sections.reason: Three of our largest repair stations are now inside emission control areas where the volatile organic compound allowance for a booth is being cut by half over four years. The solvent-borne primer currently qualified for repair work is the single largest contributor to their booth emissions, and two stations have said they will have to refuse lower shell work rather than exceed the allowance. This is a facility constraint rather than an airworthiness one, but the effect on an operator whose repair station stops taking the work is the same.
sections.description: The proposal is to qualify a water-borne epoxy primer for the same repair applications as the current scheme, with the same surface preparation and the same topcoat. The stringer assembly D5120114685540 and the right-hand stiffener DUD740691-36 would be re-identified because their supplied protection changes, and the silicone edging grommet LN198503-8B would be re-qualified for compatibility since it sits in the wet area of the joint. Qualification would cover the belly fairing areas in zones 181, 183 and 191, which is where the volume of repair work is. The cure schedule is longer than the solvent-borne primer by about ninety minutes, which the stations say they can absorb.
sections.effects: No mass change. No electrical effect except at bonding lands, where the water-borne primer behaves differently and the local removal requirement would have to be restated. Interchangeable at the structure level with the existing schemes. Booth emissions from a representative lower shell repair fall by about sixty per cent. The main cost is qualification time, not embodiment.
sections.embodiment_note: This is a process proposal with no hardware and no aircraft embodiment. If accepted it becomes available at the date of the manual revision, exactly as the current scheme did.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether this is a separate scheme or a variant of the chromate-free scheme already frozen, whether the two can share a qualification programme, what the different bonding behaviour means for the repair drawings, and whether any operator would be left with three qualified schemes to control.
